newsitem.title: USA: Washington state Gov. signs school funding bills.
newsitem.headline: Washington state Gov. signs school funding bills.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke signed three measures on Tuesday to boost public school construction and help school districts raise money.
The following bills were signed by Locke:

* Senate Bill 6045 will provide more state funds to build and modernize school buildings across Washington. As a result of the measure, $12 million would be available for school construction and $39 million for school technology in the 1997-1999 budget period, Locke said.

* House Bill 2069 authorizes school districts to ask local voters to approve levies equivalent to an additional 4.0 percent of their current state and federal funding. The additional levies would be phased in over two years.
* House Bill 2011 would allow school levies to cover periods of up to four years instead of the current maximum of two years. The proposal must still be approved by state voters in November.
